title: Mapping-space composition is associative and unital up to homotopy
statement:
Use small quasicategories, equivalence edges, right-pinched mapping spaces as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a fixed sufficiently large universe. A simplicial homotopy from $r:A\to B$ to $s:A\to B$ is a map $A\times\Delta^1\to B$ restricting to $r,s$ at the endpoints; homotopy classes below use this relation for Kan targets. For a quasicategory $\mathcal D$ write $M(a,b)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(a,b)$ and let $j_{a,b}:M(a,b)\to U(a,b)$ be the specified homotopy equivalence to the arrow mapping space in [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. Define $V(a,b,d)$ in degree $n$ to be the maps $\Delta^2\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal D$ whose restrictions to the three vertex factors are constant at $a,b,d$, with operators by restriction in $\Delta^n$. Let $\theta:V(a,b,d)\to U(b,d)\times U(a,b)$ restrict to the edges $12,01$, in that order, and let $\ell:V(a,b,d)\to U(a,d)$ restrict to $02$. Then $V(a,b,d)$ is Kan and $\theta$ is a homotopy equivalence. The canonical composition class on the right-pinched spaces is characterized by
$$[j_{a,d}]\,c_{a,b,d}=[\ell]\,[\theta]^{-1}([j_{b,d}]\times[j_{a,b}]),\qquad c_{a,b,d}:M(b,d)\times M(a,b)\longrightarrow M(a,d).$$
These canonical composition classes are associative and unital up to simplicial homotopy: for four vertices $a,b,d,e$, the two composites from $M(d,e)\times M(b,d)\times M(a,b)$ to $M(a,e)$ are homotopic, and composing either side with the vertex represented by a degenerate identity edge is homotopic to the identity map. On components they give an ordinary category $h\mathcal D$ whose objects are the vertices and whose morphisms are $\pi_0M(a,b)$, with identities represented by degenerate edges. Every component is represented by an edge, and a $2$-simplex with edges $u:a\to b$, $v:b\to d$, $w:a\to d$ gives $[v][u]=[w]$. An edge $u:a\to b$ has invertible component class if and only if there is an edge $v:b\to a$ and $2$-simplices with boundary triples $(u,v,\mathrm{id}_a)$ and $(v,u,\mathrm{id}_b)$; thus it is precisely an equivalence edge in the definition cited above. Precomposition and postcomposition by an edge are restrictions of this canonical composition class to its vertex; they depend only on its component class.

source.place: Subsection Composition of Morphisms (Kerodon 01PF): Corollaries 4.6.8.5 and 4.6.8.8 (fixed-vertex strings), Construction 4.6.8.9 (composition), Remark 4.6.8.10 (components), Propositions 4.6.8.11 and 4.6.8.12 (unitality and associativity), Remark 4.6.8.14 (ordinary homotopy category), and Notation 4.6.8.15 (pre/postcomposition). Definition 1.4.6.1 and Remarks 1.4.6.6 and 1.4.6.8 identify invertibility with inverse-triangle witnesses. The right-pinched model and its specified inclusion are those of lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison. These are Kerodon references, not Stacks tags. Read online; archive WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: By the degreewise definition of the right-pinched mapping space and of the internal functor simplicial set, the simplicial set $V(a,b,d)$ is exactly the multiarrow fiber $H_{\mathcal D}(a,b,d)$ of [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine]. Its consecutive-edge fibers are the arrow mapping spaces $U(b,d)$ and $U(a,b)$ (in the displayed order), and restriction to those edges is precisely $\theta$. The right-pinched and arrow models are related by the natural maps $j_{x,y}$ of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison].

source.place: Construction 4.6.8.9 and Corollary 4.6.8.5, identifying fixed-vertex multiarrow fibers and their consecutive-edge restriction

proof.text: By [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine], $p=\theta$ has the right lifting property against every boundary inclusion. By the relative boundary-cell filtration of [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells], this implies lifting against every simplicial monomorphism: extend over each attached simplex using boundary lifting, and take the compatible union of the lifts. The target $Y=U(b,d)\times U(a,b)$ is Kan by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], since a product horn is filled coordinatewise. For a horn in $V$, first fill its image in $Y$ and then lift along the horn inclusion; hence $V$ is Kan. Lift $\varnothing\hookrightarrow Y$ against $p$ to obtain a section $s:Y\to V$. On $V\times\partial\Delta^1$ prescribe $sp$ and $1_V$, and use $p\operatorname{pr}_V$ as the map $V\times\Delta^1\to Y$; lifting the endpoint inclusion gives $sp\simeq1_V$, while $ps=1_Y$. Thus $p$ is a simplicial homotopy equivalence. This argument also covers an empty target. Horns, boundaries and products have the meanings in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the spine statement.

source.place: Corollary 4.6.8.5, the trivial Kan fibration on the spine, with the Kan mapping-space models of Construction 4.6.5.1 and Proposition 4.6.5.5

proof.text: For the homotopy-class calculus used here and below, [lem-cbc-kan-mapping-homotopy-invariance] applied to $u=1_A$ gives that $\operatorname{Fun}(A,Z)$ is Kan whenever $Z$ is Kan. Reversing an edge there by filling an outer $2$-horn with a degenerate identity, and concatenating two edges by filling an inner $2$-horn, show that simplicial homotopy is an equivalence relation. Composing maps or taking products of homotopies preserves it, by composing their defining cylinders or pairing them.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.3.4, with the elementary outer/inner 2-horn reversal and concatenation arguments

proof.text:
Put $C_{a,b,d}=[\ell][\theta]^{-1}$, the arrow-space composition class of [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine]. Write $J_{x,y}=[j_{x,y}]$ and $K_{x,y}=J_{x,y}^{-1}$, using [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. Then set
$$c_{a,b,d}=K_{a,d}C_{a,b,d}(J_{b,d}\times J_{a,b}).$$
Multiplication on the left by $J_{a,d}$ proves the displayed characterization. Any other class with that characterization is equal to this one after multiplication by $K_{a,d}$, so no choice of inverse changes it. All these are classes of actual simplicial maps.

source.place: Construction 4.6.8.9 (composition by the long edge), together with Proposition 4.6.5.10 (right-pinch equivalence)

proof.text:
Apply the face/degeneracy coherence clause of [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine] to the arrow spaces. With $C,J,K$ as in steps 3–4, its associativity and $JK=1$ give the explicit equalities of homotopy classes
$$\begin{aligned}
J_{a,e}c_{a,d,e}(1\times c_{a,b,d})
 &=C_{a,d,e}(1\times C_{a,b,d})(J_{d,e}\times J_{b,d}\times J_{a,b}),\\
J_{a,e}c_{a,b,e}(c_{b,d,e}\times1)
 &=C_{a,b,e}(C_{b,d,e}\times1)(J_{d,e}\times J_{b,d}\times J_{a,b}).
\end{aligned}$$
The right sides agree by that clause, so multiplication by $K_{a,e}$ gives the asserted associativity. The explicit degree-zero pinch map of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] is the identity on edges, hence sends each degenerate identity vertex $i_x$ to that same identity vertex. The two arrow-space unit equations therefore give
$$J_{a,b}c_{a,a,b}(1\times i_a)=J_{a,b},\qquad J_{a,b}c_{a,b,b}(i_b\times1)=J_{a,b}.$$
Cancel $J_{a,b}$ for both unit conclusions. These equalities of classes give actual simplicial homotopies by the Kan functor-space observation in steps 3–4, using [lem-cbc-kan-mapping-homotopy-invariance].

source.place: Propositions 4.6.8.11 and 4.6.8.12, and Notation 4.6.8.15 (units, associativity, and pre/postcomposition)

proof.text: Precomposition and postcomposition are restrictions of $c$ to the selected input vertex. Vertices in the same component of a Kan mapping space can be joined by one oriented edge: reverse edges by outer $2$-horn fillers with a degenerate identity, and combine a finite edge chain by inner $2$-horn fillers. The identification of realization components with edge-chain components is [lem-coef-kan-realization-serre]. If $q:\Delta^1\to M(a,b)$ joins $u$ to $u'$, evaluating a representative of $c$ on $(z,q(t))$ gives a cylinder homotopy from precomposition by $u$ to precomposition by $u'$; evaluating on $(q(t),z)$ proves the postcomposition assertion. No inverse-edge hypothesis is needed for this component dependence.

source.place: Notation 4.6.8.15; the component-dependence cylinder is written explicitly

proof.text: By the degreewise mapping-space definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], vertices of $M(a,b)$ are exactly edges $a\to b$. By [lem-coef-kan-realization-serre], every component is an edge-chain component and therefore has such a vertex. For a $2$-simplex $\sigma$ with edges $(u,v,w)$, its vertex in $V$ satisfies $\theta(\sigma)=(v,u)$ and $\ell(\sigma)=w$. Applying $\pi_0$ to $[\ell]=C[\theta]$ and using that the pinch maps fix edges proves $[v][u]=[w]$ for the composition of step 4, using [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine] and [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. The associativity and unit homotopies of step 5 now give the ordinary category on these component sets.

source.place: Remark 4.6.8.10 and Remark 4.6.8.14 (components and homotopy category); Kerodon 004Q, Definition 1.4.6.1 and Remarks 1.4.6.6 and 1.4.6.8 (inverse triangles), with the explicit inner 3-horn argument written here.

proof.text: It remains to prove the inverse-triangle implication, rather than merely equality of composite components. Suppose $[u]$ is invertible and choose an edge $v:b\to a$ representing its inverse. For either ordered pair $(f,g)=(u,v)$ or $(f,g)=(v,u)$, put $x=\operatorname{source}(f)$ and $y=\operatorname{target}(f)$. Fill the inner $2$-horn $(f,g)$ in $\mathcal D$ to obtain a triangle $(f,g,w)$ on $(x,y,x)$. The established composition rule gives $[w]=[\mathrm{id}_x]$. By the component and Kan observations of step 6, choose an oriented edge in $M(x,x)$ from $\mathrm{id}_x$ to $w$. The right-pinched degree-one definition identifies it with a triangle $(\mathrm{id}_x,w,\mathrm{id}_x)$ on $(x,x,x)$: its $02$ edge is its initial endpoint and its $12$ edge is its final endpoint. On vertices $(x,x,y,x)$ take face $123$ to be $(f,g,w)$, face $013$ to be this homotopy triangle, and face $012$ to be the degenerate triangle $(\mathrm{id}_x,f,f)$. Their shared edges agree, so they define an inner horn $\Lambda^3_1\to\mathcal D$. A filler, provided by the quasicategory definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], has face $023$ with edges $(f,g,\mathrm{id}_x)$. Applying this one construction to both ordered pairs gives the two required inverse triangles with the same edge $v$. Conversely, two such triangles give both inverse equations by the established component composition rule. This proves the claimed equivalence with the definition of equivalence edge.

source.place: Remark 4.6.8.10 and Remark 4.6.8.14 (components and homotopy category); Kerodon 004Q, Definition 1.4.6.1 and Remarks 1.4.6.6 and 1.4.6.8 (inverse triangles), with the explicit inner 3-horn argument written here.
